utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You said you were taken to room 16, then you spent a short while in Room 18 before being taken to building number 1. Can you remember when that was and on which floor you were?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was all in 1992. I cannot remember the dates and months. We spent a very long time precisely in that room in building number 1, and that's the building from which we were taken to the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said in 1992, was it autumn, winter? Can you try to remember the month?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was August or September approximately. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If you can remember, what room was it? If not, then on which floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Room 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to explain, you said, "We were taken." Was the entire work platoon taken with you to Room 13?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When there were problems related to taking people to work, they probably wanted to avoid taking people out from different rooms, so we were all put into one room. We spent a very short while in Room 16, and then we were all transferred to Room 13. There may have been exceptional cases when somebody was taken out from a different room, but that happened by chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So from August or September, most of those who worked were in the same room with you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With a proviso that some people -- few of them, though, were in different rooms, and were taken out as required.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But beginning with August or September 1992, Room 13 was the working room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said before yes, but approximately. I don't know how to put it. I don't remember it that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said you started to work about a month or so after you were brought to the KP Dom. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you were told that you were going to work, did you refuse? Did you rebel? Did you express any disapproval?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that to rebel or to express disapproval would have been a big risk. It didn't occur to me to refuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mentioned Dule or Dusan who worked in the metalwork shop. Do you know by any chance when he started to work and for how long he worked in the metal shop?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think practically throughout, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From time when you came until the moment when you left the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were there any tinsmiths or welders in the metalwork shop?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were various profiles of metal workers, from welders, mechanics, locksmiths, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that you did whatever was needed, that you repaired vehicles, that you did all kinds of jobs related to servicing of vehicles, changing oil, repairs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is completely correct, all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So, sir, you did all the repairs required on vehicles, but the only thing you were defending -- you were defended to repair was the exhaust pipe on the kedi vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it was defended or they didn't have it, I don't know, because there were other cases when repairs were required on other vehicles but we couldn't do it because there were no spare parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You are a mechanic. Do you mean to tell me that an exhaust pipe with a hole in it cannot be repaired? You have a tinsmith and you have a welder. Do you mean to say that you cannot just fix it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can be patched.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But for this particular car, they did not tell you to patch the exhaust pipe?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many vehicles, speaking about proper technical working order, were not up to snuff. They had various faults.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does that mean that there were other vehicles with faulty exhaust pipes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying specifically that it was all cars, but there were about -- there were some with faulty exhaust pipes which had holes in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I didn't understand what you said about 16.

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sixteen is a freight vehicle. Sixteen was a reference to its tonnage and it was driven by Miso Krsmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you mean it was often driven, does it mean that this person frequently took it out of the KP Dom and brought it back?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a vehicle which belonged to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And it also had a faulty exhaust pipe?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, you told us yesterday that the fishpond in Jelec, as far as you knew, was emptied. Are you aware that there is a fishpond at Bukovica near Mjesaja?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm very aware of that

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you aware that part of the fish from Jelec were transferred to Bukovica near Mjesaja?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that one morning you noticed this kedi vehicle washed. Can you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to remember that date because it's been a long time, and I'm starting to forget even names and surnames and nicknames, let alone remember exact dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I would appreciate it, sir, if you could tell us to the best of your memory, if not the date, then the month when you saw that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately about a month or two months after my arrival, approximately within that time frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mean after your arrival?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, after I was taken out. Please don't pin me down to dates, because I started to be taken out from the KP Dom to the metalwork shop at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So, sir, you mean to say a month or two after you were taken out to the metalwork shop?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying approximately. It can vary. It's perhaps a month sooner or later. You're asking me to say something that I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You are a witness here and we are discussing a very important matter. I don't want to insist that you remember something that you cannot remember, but I'm just asking you to tell us to the best of your memory when approximately you saw that vehicle washed.

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said. A month or a month and a half later, and even that is not a time frame I can swear to. But if you insist, let it be a month later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So counting from your arrival to the KP Dom, that would be two or three months later?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two months, two to three months at the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So that would make it the end of August, early September?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. In any case, it would be before that. Let us see. May, June. That could have been August, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Tell me, please, since it was a month after you started working, how many times did you wash that car before that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, too, is a difficult question to answer, how many times I worked on the kedi, how many times I worked on the vehicle 16 or vehicle 20, or the vehicle FAP. I cannot say. It's a long period. I cannot say how many times I had to deal with a particular vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I asked you, sir, how many times before the time when you saw it washed did you wash it yourself?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We washed it and we oiled it and lubricated it and changed the oil and did all the work that needed to be done on all the vehicles of the KP Dom. We were the only ones who had to do that work. I cannot remember how many times I did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you ever wash this kedi at all before you saw it washed?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We washed all vehicles, not only that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you saw that vehicle washed, did you see any traces of blood there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was just passing by. I only saw a vehicle freshly washed. I couldn't see any blood. We were just passing by on our way to the metalwork shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On that day when you saw that washed kedi, did you work normally in the metalwork shop as on any other day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All the people who normally worked in the metalwork shop, you worked normally throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember about everyone, but it was a regular working day for us. I don't know whether it was the same for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you remember who was next to you when you were passing by that car?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a very difficult question to which I cannot give an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You mentioned Miso Krsmanovic, if I remember correctly, a driver, and you mentioned that you prepared the vehicle for the road. Whose driver was Miso Krsmanovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miso Krsmanovic used to drive the 1620 freight vehicle, and whether there was somebody in that vehicle with him, I cannot know; where he went, who was with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did Miso Krsmanovic travel frequently?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And another driver, his last name is Milic. I cannot remember the first name. The two of them took turns on that 1620 vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did these men also drive the red 128 that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that with any certainty, but I saw that vehicle when it came to the metalwork shop to be serviced for tyres to be pumped up, et cetera. That vehicle was brought to us because Mr. Krnojelac never contacted with us, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So Krsmanovic and Milic would bring that red 128 vehicle to be prepared for the road?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You misunderstood me. I was speaking about the 1620 vehicle, and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. these men -- in fact, it was mainly the chief of the metalwork shop, Goljanin, who brought the vehicle for servicing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Outside those occasions when it was brought to be serviced at your shop, did you have any occasion to find out where that vehicle was driven, when it went out to town?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not my job. My job was to prepare that vehicle for -- when the warden needed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you do that often, prepare the vehicle for the road for journeys?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said you serviced it almost every month.

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say not very frequently, using as a reference my journeys to Miljevina which lasted a month each. So if I take into account that I went to Miljevina three or four times and was away for a month at least each time, that means I was away from the KP Dom at least for four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While you were in Miljevina, did anyone else take care of that car?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The late Sevko Kubat. For a while, Rasim Taranin was the man. In another period it was the person under the number 144. He sometimes worked in the metalwork shop. Those were approximately the people who worked up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you repair military vehicles, vehicles of the military police?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion only, it was a Deutz vehicle. Deutz 110. It came to the compound one day, and there was an UAZ vehicle with a changed engine. It used to be a petrol engine, but it was changed. Another engine was built into it. I don't know whose property it was. I don't know whether it was owned by the army or the military police. Only one military vehicle came to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you notice outside the KP Dom a VW vehicle which also had a peculiar sound of the exhaust pipe, Volkswagon?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of those vehicles, the only one I know is the one which took me to Miljevina. It was a Golf, a Volkswagen Golf. After the warden was replaced, a new vehicle appeared, a brand new white Golf diesel, and that was the only vehicle I noticed there. And only one time did a Volkswagen Bug arrival, a Beetle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Whose was it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who the owner was, but at that moment Janic, also known as Tuta, was in the metalwork shop, and a man called Daco, and I don't know if there was anybody else who came with those vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did that vehicle have a peculiar sound of the exhaust pipe?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because it didn't come up to the metalwork shop. It stopped at the metal gate. The man alone worked to the workshop.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said yesterday during your examination-in-chief that you frequently took tyres from the waste dump, patched them, and fixed them onto cars. Do you know why you did that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there were no new tyres available. We found very few new tyres and we had to do with old ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You said in your statement that the International Red Cross brought some furnaces. Were those furnaces distributed to you? Were they distributed among the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the arrival of the International Red Cross, the furnaces were distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that Sevko Kubat died at the KP Dom. Could you tell us when that happened, which month approximately and which year?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the month or the date, but it was in 1994, perhaps four months before all of us were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So it was in 1994 that Savo Todovic reprimanded him for not working, for shirking from work?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You spoke about the Miljevina mine and how you went there in December 1992 and tried to repair some cars and make them operational. You also mentioned that a working group was formed to work at the Miljevina mine. Do you know when it was formed and when it started working?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name Todor Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I have a register of duty rosters here. Do you -- these duty rosters refer to the mine. Do you allow for the possibility that the first group went to work at the mine in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot claim because I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. When you went to Miljevina for the first time, you said Pedo and another person were with you in the vehicle. What was Pedo wearing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: A military camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did he also carry an automatic rifle?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true that you stated that you were the only one who was taken out at that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Before that, smaller groups had been taken out to disassemble some machines. All I know is that two or three men would be taken out to town which means that I was not the only one at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know when Dr. Torlak left the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date in his case, either, but it was sometime in 1993,. I think he was among the last people to leave the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it also true that you stated that you had heard that Dr. Torlak was taken to Pale?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything of this sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I will read out to you, sir, a part of your statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1995. It's page 9, one paragraph before last towards the end. "When I was in Miljevina I heard that Dr. Torlak had been taken out to be a doctor at Pale."

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember that statement now. And that's the story that did the rounds. I'm sorry, it's been a long time and that's really the statement I have given, and I could say the same thing again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you were passing through the hole behind the metal door, that is the path you had to take every day to the metalwork shop; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From the moment you started working, that is to say, 40 or 45 days after you were brought to the KP Dom; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you see blood on the walls in that hall?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not see any blood; however, what was very noticeable was lots and lots of holes in the wall from bullets that had been fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In that hall, how wide is that hall?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two and a half, three metres. It's longer than that. I'm just telling you all of this approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: However, you saw these holes on the lateral walls that are two, two and a half metres away from each other; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you see bullet holes anywhere else except in that hall?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course there were holes outside, too, on the facades, then also at the metal shop you could see lots of casings and things like that, because there was quite a bit of shooting at first. You didn't know where the shooting was coming from or who was shooting or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You talked about persons who came to your room after beatings. You mentioned a few persons. Did they tell you where they had been beaten and who had beaten them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A few people came, although most of the people who had been beaten very badly would end up in isolation cells very often, and there were some persons who were brought directly to the rooms. Never could a person mention the name of the person who had beaten that person because they were mostly masked, things like that, in most cases, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say masked, you mean that they had masks on their faces; but do you know what they wore, what kind of clothes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not explain this in detail, what kind of uniforms they were in, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yesterday you spoke about Mohamed Alikadic that you saw him at the window. At which window, which room, which floor, which part of the building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which room number that was. That is at the pavilion where we were, opposite Room 16 to the right. I think it was the last floor, in the very corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was the window open?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So he leaned across the open window and showed this to you, or what happened?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It so happened that as I was leaving the dining room I glanced at that building, the window was open. He was about a metre or a metre and a half into the room, and we knew each other very well and probably our glances met. And he just sort of signalled to me that he'd like a cigarette or a shaver, but that was impossible since he had already been in isolation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was there anybody else with him in that room on the top floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say because I did not see anybody but him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that he asked you not to tell anyone about what he had done. Did you tell anyone?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he told any other detainee?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know that as records what Alikadic did from the base to the Osanica bridge there was only Serb-held territory?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not quite aware of the separation line, but allegedly it was the Osanica bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So from the bridge towards Foca towards the KP Dom, it was Serb-held territory?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way it was supposed to have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that in that truck that he drove backwards, he had been tied to the seat. Do you know what he had been tied with?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not tell me what he had been tied with, but he said that he had been tied and buckled to the seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, you said that in the KP Dom you got pneumonia and that they had to treat you. Who treated you, and when did you get pneumonia?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pneumonia? Pneumonia? I got pneumonia -- I'm not sure. I'm not sure whether it's 1992 or 1993. I think it's the winter of 1993. I was in Miljevina. In the morning I got up and I was all feverish, and they took me back to the KP Dom. Gojko was there then, and that moment Aziz Torlak was at Gojko's and Karovic, too, and they came to the conclusion that it was pneumonia on the left side. I was prescribed penicillin injections. I don't know exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you get these penicillin shots?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who was Gojko?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the nurse who worked at the clinic in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What were Dr. Aziz Torlak and Dr. Karovic doing at his place?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what they were doing then, but that moment when I came to the office, they were there with Gojko. At Gojko's insistence that they should also listen to me through the stethoscope, they all came to the same conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How long did you take -- did you get these penicillin shots, for how long, for how many days?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said just now that I don't know exactly for how long. I think I got seven of them. I'm not sure. Every day a shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who gave you these shots? Who administered them to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely Gojko.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You went to the clinic, I presume?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went to the clinic. But again, I was always escorted by the person who was on duty in the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you see Dr. Dobrilovic or Dr. Vladicic come into the clinic at the KP Dom where Gojko worked?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, once, once. I said that we went out, so perhaps they came several times, but once I did notice them coming to the building where the KP Dom clinic was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, you talked about the transit room. This transit room at the administration building of the KP Dom, did it have any windows and which direction did these windows face?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which transit room you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You pointed out a transit room to the left of the entrance behind the room, the reception office, where the guards were?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think these windows faced the road, the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you said here that because you worked so hard at the KP Dom, your back was injured. Before the KP Dom, did you have an office job or did you also work hard before the war broke out and before you came to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was only a mechanic. But I worked at the [redacted] [redacted] all the time, and that was quite different from everything else. We had lifts and extra lifts and all the most up-to-date equipment a the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that your eyes also got weaker, your eyesight due to the KP Dom. Are you aware of the fact that in your 40s, your eyesight gets poorer, or do you think it only has to do with the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not an expert in medicine; however, I did notice that my eyesight was getting poorer, much poorer. What the reason for this is, I'm really no expert. I cannot be the judge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these were all the questions that the Defence had of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examination, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I have a few matters to clarify. First of all, I think there is a mistake in the transcript, but I didn't want to interrupt Mr. Bakrac because I want to clarify it now. On page 45, line 5 it was actually in the transcript that before his transfer to the Room 13 he was briefly in Room 16, and I think that's a mistake and I just want to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said first you were in Room 16, then you were transferred to Room 18, and finally to Room 13. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I already said that to the gentleman. I explained it to him. I don't know whether you understood what I was saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it has to be number 18 instead of number 16 as it says in the transcript, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that may or may not be so, but it doesn't matter. He's now got it sorted out.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You also mentioned this 1620 freight vehicle which also has a -- had something wrong with the exhaust pipe. The sound of this 1620 freight vehicle, was it different from the kedi, the sound that the kedi exhaust pipe made?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it was, because a freight vehicle and a passenger vehicle can never make the same kind of noise, and it can never be of the same loudness as well. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In relation to the red 128, you said that Goljanin usually brought it, brought it in when it was to be serviced by you. From where did he bring it in, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is hard to say where he brought it from because the compound of the metalwork shop is closed. I already described the door. So where could this vehicle come from? Somewhere from the outside, from the parking lot, wherever.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was there a special parking lot for the cars belonging to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Where was it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of it was right next to the KP Dom. The other part was across the street, on the other side of the road as you go towards the hospital. And also, lots of old vehicles, Furgons that were no longer used, were parked at this other end of the parking lot on the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know where the red 128 was usually parked? Did you see it on any of these parking spots that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, even if they were parked, these official vehicles and personal vehicles would usually be parked right by the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you see this red 128 being parked there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps a few times.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ever see someone else driving it except for Mr. Krnojelac and Mr. Goljanin?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never noticed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac addressed with you the bullet holes that you saw in the hall behind the metal door. Would you be able to point it out on a photo where you saw the holes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have one.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the photo 7470. That is a photo that we have already discussed with the witness. The bottom, the bottom photo, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to point to us where you saw the bullet holes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just explain. These holes had just been patched by two young men from Djidjevo. One is [redacted], the other one I don't know. You can perhaps notice a patched hole here, and I don't know where else.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone; he can no longer be heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These holes here were patched by two young men from Djidjevo. One was [redacted]; I don't know the other one. I don't know his last name, that is. And they were precisely in my room. And one day in the afternoon, it was around 12.00 or -- I don't know, I wasn't working that day. They were taken out, and they were patching these holes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is --

utterances.speaker: FWS-249 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was pointing at the wall to the right from the yellow arrow, that is, to the right from the metal door, and he was pointing at the lower, lower part of the wall, almost close to the floor. Yes, thank you. And these were the questions that the Prosecution had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir, for giving evidence. You're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, is 172 your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: From last week, yes. What are the protective measures for this Witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The witness was granted a pseudonym, image distortion, and voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, if it's going to be voice distortion, the video people like to have a special test done with him.
